overview: Rise 6.1.30's Criticals is a ModeValue shell with six modes, default Packet, and no mode sends the C02 attack itself: each mode pre-arms the conditions for the player's own clicks, and when combined with KillAura the attack stream fires AttackEvent before its C02, which is the ordering the packet modes rely on. PacketCriticals, the default, listens on AttackEvent and, gated by a 500ms StopWatch and onGroundTicks above 2, sends two C04PacketPlayerPosition lifts (posY plus 0.0625, then posY plus 0, both onGround false) through PacketUtil.send before the attack goes out, then calls onCriticalHit for the client-side particles; 0.0625 is sqrt(1/256), the vanilla yOnGround epsilon. EditCriticals spreads two sub-pixel lifts (0.0005, 0.0001, onGround false) across the two PreMotion ticks after an attack. NoGroundCriticals flips onGround false on every PreMotion, and Vulcan and Watchdog gate the same flag flip on ticksSinceVelocity (18 and 80) with FallDistanceComponent.distance below 1.8. VerusCriticals repeats the Packet sequence with a hurtTime nonzero requirement.

sections.p: The ModeValue registers six Mode instances and defaults to Packet. The packet modes (Packet, Verus) hook AttackEvent and send C04 lifts from the attack listener, so the lifts are queued before the C02 of the same click; the flag modes (NoGround, Vulcan, Watchdog) hook PreMotionEvent and only rewrite the onGround flag of the tick's own C03. Every mode gates on mc.thePlayer.onGroundTicks or equivalent local state, and the delay NumberValue (default 500ms, range 0-1000) paces the packet modes with a StopWatch. None of the modes construct C02PacketUseEntity, which is why the attack packet appears in the analysis only as the packet the module's ordering exploits.

PacketCriticals sends the two C04s back to back with onGround false: the server applies the 0.0625 lift, so the attack that follows arrives with a nonzero fall distance and crits, and the second C04 re-asserts the original y so the net displacement is zero. The 0.0625 offset is exactly the vanilla ground epsilon, the smallest lift that reads as a fall on a stock server. VerusCriticals is the same sequence with a hurtTime nonzero gate, so it only fires while the player is recovering from damage. EditCriticals is the anti-detection variant: the two lifts are 0.0005 and 0.0001, both below the 0.03 min-move, so the server ignores the coordinates but still applies the onGround false flag, spreading the claim across two ticks instead of one packet pair.

NoGroundCriticals claims onGround false on every PreMotion, which keeps the server-side fall distance permanently armed for any click while standing. Vulcan and Watchdog are velocity-aware versions: they only claim onGround false within 18 or 80 ticks of the last knockback (ticksSinceVelocity) and while FallDistanceComponent.distance stays below 1.8, so the flag spoof only runs during the window a server would accept a fall claim. FallDistanceComponent accumulates per-tick vertical deltas at very low priority and resets on an onGround claim, which gives the modes a shared distance state without touching the vanilla fallDistance field.

files.label: Criticals.java
files.explanation: The dispatcher is a ModeValue with six registered modes and a Packet default, with no logic of its own. The analysis embeds it to show the registered mode set and the default, because the mechanism splits between the attack-listener packet modes and the pre-motion flag modes, and the mode list is what determines which countering checks apply to a given configuration.

files.label: PacketCriticals.java (default mode)
files.explanation: The default mode carries the exact wire sequence: two C04PacketPlayerPosition packets at posY plus 0.0625 and posY plus 0, both onGround false, sent from the AttackEvent listener through PacketUtil.send, which places them ahead of the C02 of the same click. The StopWatch delay and the onGroundTicks gate above 2 are the pacing constraints, and the onCriticalHit call is purely cosmetic. This file is the whole packet-crit mechanism in 33 lines and the mode a default configuration exposes to the countering checks.

countering.label: fight.Critical (fall-distance divergence)
countering.explanation: NoCheatPlus runs this check whenever the server sees a crit. Rule one resets on water, webs, climbables and slow-fall; rule two requires a legitimate jump phase (sfJumpPhase within 1 and the lift-off envelope's max jump phase, no collision above) so an early jump crit flags; rule three is the packet-crit killer: |ncpFallDistance - mcFallDistance| over 1e-5 while moveInfo.from.isOnGround() or the touched-ground workaround is set raises data.criticalVL by 1. The 0.0625 lift makes the server's fall distance positive while NCP's own accounting, which never observed a jump, stays at zero, so the divergence rule flags the very first packet-crit attack. The honest gap is EditCriticals: its 0.0005 and 0.0001 offsets sit below the 0.03 min-move, the server ignores the coordinates, mcFallDistance never arms, and the divergence never materializes, so sub-pixel modes pass this check by construction.

countering.label: Criticals (grounded-attack gate)
countering.explanation: Arc v2 derives ground from its own physics state rather than the packet: on attack, data.isOnGround() (fed by its MovingListener) combined with a vertical speed below 0.37 raises "critical while onGround". A real jump launches at 0.42, so the bound separates genuine jumps from every lift a packet-crit module can produce. The 0.0625 lift moves the entity 0.0625 blocks, the Edit lifts move it by fractions of a milliblock, and the flag-only modes move it not at all, so all six Rise modes attack while Arc still considers the player grounded and flag on the first swing. This is the simplest counter in the set and the reason the module's own gate (onGroundTicks above 2) cannot help: the module needs the player grounded to attack, and Arc reads grounded from the same physics.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (vertical envelope)
countering.explanation: SurvivalFly's vertical allowance comes from vDistRel, seeded by the previous move's momentum, and accepts only zero-y moves on ground, real jumps, step-ups and riptide launches; ground is derived from a block-cache ray trace, never the packet flag. A C04 lift presents a 0.0625 yDistance with no jump momentum, so yDistanceAboveLimit turns positive and the violation (max(hDistanceAboveLimit, 0) + max(yDistanceAboveLimit, 0)) * 100 reverts the move, and the onGround false claim does not relax the envelope because NCP's own trace says the position is grounded. The same mechanism catches the NoGround flag stream's position-bearing ticks if the client ever couples them with a y delta, while the pure sub-0.03 offsets of EditCriticals stay under the envelope's resolution, which is the same min-move blind spot that defeats the divergence rule.

countering.label: SmallHop (mini-hop detector)
countering.explanation: Hawk's SmallHop exists specifically because tiny jumps bypass speed and criticals checks: it flags a move that starts grounded with deltaY between 0 and 0.4 while the previous deltaY was nonpositive, no accepted knockback, no slime or ladder and no adjacent solid, and the predicted destination is not really on the ground, then punishes and rubber-bands. The 0.0625 packet lift is a textbook small hop and trips it immediately. The design tolerance is the escape hatch for the Edit mode: offsets at or below 0.001 fall inside the check's ground tolerance and pass, which matches the module's own constant choices (0.0005, 0.0001) and is the honest both-sides statement for the sub-pixel variants.
